beats.narration_text: These six formulas come from Ruben Hassid at how-to-ai.guide. Each one has the rule, what you're doing right now that's wrong, the exact thing to copy, the math behind why it works, and where to apply it. Let's go through them one by one.

card.sub: Rule · You right now · Copy this · The math · Where. From Ruben Hassid / how-to-ai.guide.

beats.narration_text: Formula one: Delete your About Me file. Right now you probably have a twenty-two-thousand-word file Claude re-reads before every task. Instead: turn it into a Skill. Invoke /about-me only when needed. The math: files load every session, skills load on demand. Where: Cowork, Customize, Skills. Formula two: Skills plus Projects, nothing else. A hundred skills should be two projects. Teach Claude a skill, use it inside a project. Skills travel to any chat. Projects never poison other chats. Use the left menu.

beats.narration_text: Formula three: No settings is the best setting. Right now you probably have instructions in every box and get the same answer every time. Instead: turn everything off except Connectors. Keep Global Instructions empty. The math: too much context equals Claude going in circles. Two minutes in Settings. Formula four: Make Claude ask you. Right now you're writing five-hundred-word prompts, badly. Instead, use this exact prompt: 'I want [task] to [goal]. Ask me questions with AskUserQuestion first.' The math: five-hundred words cost five-hundred tokens per re-read. Clicks cost nothing. Use this everywhere and follow up with it forever.

beats.narration_text: Formula five: Fable on Low, Opus on High. Right now you're paying for the smartest AI to rewrite an email. Instead: use Fable 5 on Low for hard problems, two turns maximum. Opus 4.8 on High for everything else — it's included. The math: Fable is fifteen cents a question, Opus 4.8 is fourteen dollars for a long session. Use the model picker plus the effort toggle. Formula six: Edit, don't follow up. Right now you're sending 'No, I meant…' on top of twenty-nine old messages. Instead: click Edit on your prompt. Everything after it disappears. The math: message thirty costs thirty-one times message one. This applies everywhere — yes, Cowork too.

beats.narration_text: The single formula that changes the most: Make Claude ask you. Stop writing long prompts. Write a short one and let AskUserQuestion pull out what Claude needs. Clicks cost almost nothing. Your five-hundred-word prompt costs five-hundred tokens on every single re-read of that conversation.

card.sub: 'I want [task] to [goal]. Ask me questions with AskUserQuestion first.' Short prompt. Click answers. Saves every session.

beats.narration_text: And the one formula that immediately changes your token bill: Edit, don't follow up. Every 'no I meant' you send stacks on top of the whole conversation. Click Edit on your original prompt instead. The old exchange gets replaced, not piled on. Message thirty is thirty-one times more expensive than message one — author's calculation, but the direction is undeniably real.

card.sub: Click Edit on your prompt — old exchange replaced, not stacked. Message 30 costs 31× message 1 (author's claim). Works in Cowork too.

beats.narration_text: Quick note on the pricing in formula five: Fable at fifteen cents a question and Opus at fourteen dollars for a long session — these are Ruben's stated figures at the time he wrote this. Pricing changes. Check the current model picker before you build a workflow around the cost difference.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick one formula to install this week. If you use Cowork daily: delete your About Me file and rebuild it as a Skill. If you use Chat mostly: start every session with 'Ask me questions with AskUserQuestion first.' If you keep hitting limits: click Edit instead of sending a follow-up. One formula, this week. You will feel the difference by Friday.

card.sub: Cowork daily → delete About Me, make it a Skill. Chat user → AskUserQuestion on every session. Hitting limits → Edit, not follow-up.
